raw_graphql_pull_request.body: ## Purpose Make the DeepSeek-V4.1 fused all-reduce + mHC token cap configurable through `--kernel-config '{"mhc_overlap_max_tokens": N}'`. **The default stays 16, so behaviour is unchanged unless the knob is set.** `MHC_OVERLAP_MAX_TOKENS` (#57603, #57643, #58586) was tuned on GB200 and hardcoded at 16. With DSpark k=5 every sequence verifies 6 tokens, so 16 covers only two sequences, and anything larger runs the unfused path. The same cap sizes the Lamport buffer, gates the overlap path, and drives the MoE top-k finalize deferral, so it is one engine-config property. It is read per engine from `KernelConfig`, validated (`> 0`), and hashed with the rest of the kernel config, instead of being an import-time constant. I am **not** proposing a new default. #57643 reports that extending fusion to 24-128 tokens regressed model-forward time on GB200, and I could not reproduce that on B300. The numbers below are meant to show the knob is useful on at least one platform and to ask whether a per-platform or per-spec-decode default is wanted. ## Test Plan Kernel correctness above 16 tokens, on 4x B300 (TP4), CuTe DSL fused all-reduce + mHC and the finalize path against the unfused torch reference, eager, CUDA-graph replay and replay after in-place input changes: `tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py::test_all_reduce_mhc_matches_unfused_path` is now parametrized over cap 16 (existing sizes) and cap 128 (sizes 1, 6, 12, 16, 17, 20, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128, 33, 5, 128, 1). ## Test Result Correctness (B300 x4): cap 16: 264 checks, 0 failures. Cap 128: 528 checks, 0 failures at every size including 17 and 20, where #57643 reported failures in its baseline's native top-k check. The parametrized test passes under pytest on 4x B300 (`2 passed`, cap16 and cap128); a standalone harness running the same checks gave the counts above. Decode speed, B300 TP4, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, ~50k-token real source-code prefix (prefix-cached), closed-loop streams, p50 decode tok/s/user, two alternating runs per arm, 0 request errors. Noise between repeated arms is about +/-3-5%. No speculative decoding (tokens per step = concurrency), cap 128 vs 16: | Concurrency | 8k context | 51k context | |---|---|---| | 16 (fused in both) | -1.8% | +1.5% | | 24 | +8.1% | +11.8% | | 48 | +5.6% | +8.8% | | 96 | inconclusive (one stalled run) | -1.3% | DSpark k=5, adaptive verification off (6 tokens per sequence), 51k context: | Sequences | 2 (12 tok) | 4 (24) | 8 (48) | 10 (60) | 16 (96) | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | cap 128 vs 16 | +0.4% | +12.6% | +7.5% | +13.2% | +13.6% | DSpark k=5, adaptive verification on (the serving default), 51k context: | Sequences | 2 | 4 | 8 | 10 | 16 | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | cap 128 vs 16 | -2.8% | -1.6% | +2.0% | +2.7% | +6.5% | With adaptive verification on, the optimizer avoids the larger shapes, so the realized gain is smaller than the raw step-time gain. Not measured here: GB200/GB300 (the platform #57643 measured), accuracy evals above 16 tokens (the kernel check is bitwise against the unfused path, but I did not run GSM8K/GPQA with the cap raised), and any model other than DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. ## AI assistance This PR was prepared by Claude Code on behalf of the submitter. The B300 measurements and kernel correctness runs above were executed through it on B300 nodes. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01A9Ef2S3fbtzAiwj1cT6NR2 --- Need help on this PR?
